title: Ask Search Anything (Google)
arc: ladder: one repeating carrier sentence 'Ask ...' whose last word changes while a product demo plays behind the changing word (simple questions -> longer questions -> guide you -> do the research -> shop for you -> tailored -> get things done -> Type it / Say it / Snap it / Film it -> Ask anything), then collapses to the G.
world: Pale cool-white ground, hairline Google colours (blue, red, yellow, green) only as soft gradients and glows, thin Product-Sans-style type with one word at a time coloured; real product UI always shown tilted in perspective as a floating sheet.
actor: The carrier line 'Ask it to ...': a small black sentence at the top of the frame that restates the stem and swaps the final word, plus the search bar/pill and colour glow edges around product cards.

lines.show: 'Now' appears in blue-teal, 'you' and 'can' append in black, the line shrinks as it fades; the stem is set small so the next word can be large.
lines.handoff: The stem dissolves; the next word comes at the same spot.

lines.show: 'Ask' pops in black, 'Search' appends in blue-purple; both small; then the line shrinks.
lines.handoff: 'anything' scales up past the stem as the stem vanishes.

lines.show: 'anything' is set very large, letters arriving 'any' then 'anythin' then 'anything', coloured by a blue-to-purple gradient through the 'y'; then greys out as sweeps of colour wipe in from the lower left.
lines.handoff: The colour sweep forms the multi-colour bands that reveal the logo.

lines.show: Diagonal ribbons in blue, purple, red, yellow and green sweep across, resolving into the Google wordmark above a white search bar; the bar settles to a thin row.
lines.handoff: The wordmark and the bar fade to a pale ground, and the small 'Ask' stem returns.

lines.show: 'Ask' appears, 'simple' lights in green, then 'questions' appends; the stem stays tiny and centred; the word 'simple' is the only coloured one.
lines.handoff: The line collapses upward as the search bar rises under it.

lines.handoff: The stem 'Ask' returns at the centre as the bar disappears.

lines.show: 'Even 3 questions' where the 3 counts 3, 9, 10 as a rolling digit; 'in 1' appends and 'question' lights blue; one row of text, no object.
lines.handoff: The text fades and the search bar with mic and lens icons slides in from the right.

lines.handoff: The AI Mode pill shrinks into the bar of the Google home page, which fills with a long query.

lines.show: 'Ask it' then 'to' then 'guide' in blue then 'you'; the long line holds one beat and fades.

lines.handoff: The arc closes into a rounded square for the next verb.

lines.show: 'Snap it' sits in a rounded-square camera frame with a rainbow stroke that pulses and then shrinks.
lines.handoff: The square rounds into a circle for the next verb.

lines.handoff: The circle opens into a pill and the line types.

lines.handoff: The pill collapses to a dash.

lines.show: The pill collapses into a short red dash, a yellow bend, a green hook and blue arm which assemble into the Google G on white; held for the last 3 seconds.
lines.handoff: End hold.

techniques: one stem sentence 'Ask it to ...' with a swapped last word
product sheet tilted in perspective as a floating card
one coloured word per phrase (simple, guide, research, shop, tailored, done)
container morph (bar -> arc -> square -> circle -> pill) for Type/Say/Snap/Film
pill collapses to a logo glyph
real prompt text typed in full
lessons: Build the film on one repeating stem and swap only the last word; the demo that follows is the proof of that word.
Colour exactly one word per phrase and keep the rest black; the colour tells the viewer which verb the next demo will prove.
Show real UI, tilted as a floating sheet, with an edge glow rather than a flat screenshot; scroll it, don't cut it.
Type out the real prompt (and let the answer status ticks run) so the viewer sees the work happening.
Compress the end: each input mode (type, say, snap, film) is the same container morphing shape, not four new scenes.
Finish by collapsing the last pill into the brand mark and hold, no tagline.
